mainEntity.name: Does this include water from food and other beverages?

acceptedAnswer.text: The total-water figure includes everything; the headline "from drinks" figure is about 80% of it, since food typically supplies around 20%. Drinks include plain water, milk, tea, coffee and other beverages — not only water.

mainEntity.name: Can I drink too much water?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, though it's uncommon — drinking very large amounts in a short period can dilute sodium in the blood, a condition called hyponatremia. It's mainly a risk during long endurance events when people drink far more than they sweat.

mainEntity.name: Is the "8 glasses a day" rule accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Eight 8-oz glasses (about 1.9 L) is a simple rule of thumb rather than an official recommendation. The National Academies reference for drinks is higher for most adults — about 9 cups for women and 13 for men — though needs vary with activity, climate and diet.
